speakers: Nicole Kajin (founder, Alpha Quest, short-term CTA)
summary: Nicole Kajin (Alpha Quest) argues Fed/political support and a Buffett ratio above 200% pushed platforms and CTAs toward hidden negative-skew and levered positioning. She treats skew and convexity, not Sharpe, as the true risk metric. Her approach trades short-term breakouts in vol-compressed markets and plans to short crowded high-Sharpe single-stock factors.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: all is well in trend following land with all the stock gen CTA indices posting gains so far in October
claims.claim: SG CTA indices were all positive in October 2025, a data point on trend-following health.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: it became clear for the political system the governance in governance in America that uh markets needed uh more support and uh more guidelines
claims.claim: Since 1987 (then 2001-03 and the GFC) US political and Fed intervention in markets has grown after each crisis, changing how markets behave.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the stock market is about 70% of the size of GDP. Today we we're over 200%.
claims.claim: With market cap/GDP (Buffett ratio) over 200% vs a 70% norm, the stock market drives the economy, so Fed and politicians act whenever it corrects (a Fed put).
claims.direction: equity drawdowns get supported by liquidity
claims.testable: yes - ratio and Fed reaction to drawdowns can be measured

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the stock market has gone from being the risky asset with high returns to effectively becoming a new fixed income
claims.claim: Because policy supports every dip, investors treat equities as risk-free fixed income, so equity risk is under-priced and positioning is crowded.
claims.testable: partly - risk perception hard to measure

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: The US is about 60% of global stocks today.
claims.claim: US weight (about 60% of global equities, with the top 7 tech stocks about 40% of US cap) shows extreme concentration of the market in one country and a few names.
claims.indicator: US share of global market cap; top-7 share of S&P

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: In that context, trend followers have been the have had a headwind.
claims.claim: Political suppression of volatility, inflation and drawdowns shortens and reverses trends, which has been a headwind for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: you see you start to hear that there's a debasing trade going on
claims.claim: Looking only at 40 years of data suggests money can be printed without consequence, but longer history shows consequences, and a dollar debasement trade is emerging.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the surrogate factor that explains all these alphas is not skill but tail risk exposure
claims.claim: The high Sharpe of large multi-manager platforms is explained by tail-risk (negative skew) exposure, not manager skill.
claims.testable: yes - test Sharpe against skew/tail exposure

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: they're actually all highly correlated to each other and to the market
claims.claim: PM alphas look uncorrelated locally, but in stress they are highly correlated to each other and to the market because they share the same tail exposure.
claims.indicator: correlation of pod PM returns in stress

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: that mean reversion is the the real bubble that would say that there's a the confidence to buy the dips
claims.claim: The real bubble is confidence that everything mean reverts and converges (buy the dips, long-short equity), so markets are priced as if equilibrium is stable forever.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: they say yeah that's not that interesting we we typically look for one sharp and above as a minimum
claims.claim: Allocators now demand Sharpe of 1 or more regardless of correlation, so a diversifying 0.7 Sharpe macro strategy is rejected, rewarding hidden tail risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I wonder if it's just part of a bigger cycle
claims.claim: Political involvement in central banking may not be unprecedented but part of a longer cycle that will clear at some point.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: There's no way you can have this amount of debt and not end up uh and continuing to print money without uh without inflation as a stabilizer.
claims.claim: Current debt levels with continued money printing mean an inflationary cycle is certain, as one of the cycle's normal phases.
claims.testable: no - not falsifiable in short run

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if you take the delta 1 markets and you hedge more and more principal components of risk, you will end up with things that have less trends but are more mean reverting in nature
claims.claim: Because investors reward high Sharpe, managers hedge out principal components of risk, producing less trending, more mean-reverting, less liquid books that need more leverage.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if delta 1 markets on trend following gives you a sharp ratio of.3 or 04
claims.claim: Delta-1 trend following has a Sharpe of about 0.3-0.4; hedged spread trading removes the trend component, which is the most macro one, to raise Sharpe.
claims.testable: yes - compare Sharpe and skew of outright vs spread books

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: PMS that are required or are being encouraged to achieve high sharp ratios are designing strategies where they're hedging 70 80 90% of the volatility
claims.claim: Single-stock pods hedge 70-90% of book volatility and are levered 20-30x, the same pattern as LTCM in fixed income, with risk looking near zero.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the slightest change in volatility, the slightest change in correlation will lead to very quick changes in liquidity
claims.claim: In highly levered hedged books, a small rise in volatility or correlation forces deleveraging and liquidity disappears quickly.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: The liquidity is provided by other PMs and the liquidity all comes in at once and all leaves at once.
claims.claim: With banks no longer committed liquidity providers, equity liquidity is supplied by other PMs and withdraws simultaneously in stress.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: you have a situation such as co and all of them are down 20 30 35% intra months although they're uncorrelated
claims.claim: In Covid (March 2020) multi-manager platforms that looked uncorrelated fell 20-35% intra-month, showing the sensitivity of leverage to a fast shock.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: creating a self reinforcing cycle in mean reversion or in convergence
claims.claim: High Sharpe attracts capital which is added to the same positions, a reflexive loop that sustains convergence trades until it breaks.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if the Fed is there to provide uh the safety net, the market put you don't have to pay for that hedge, then you're convergence trade is highly profitable for a long period of time
claims.claim: With a Fed put the tail hedge is free, so convergence/short-vol trades earn steady profit for a long time while risk builds unseen.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: Those were more organized like and gentle corrections that happened over time co happened almost too quickly for these firms to adapt.
claims.claim: The 2022, SVB, yen-carry and tariff drawdowns were gradual so pods coped; only the fast Covid shock broke them, so speed of drawdown matters.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: remember in 2022 all these partops also have trend following momentum components and momentum did very well in 2022
claims.claim: In 2022 pods were hedged by their momentum sleeves, so they needed less liquidity than in 2020.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the fact that there's been no crisis means the risk is steadily increasing
claims.claim: Absence of a crisis lets leverage, platform allocations and investor confidence grow, so latent vulnerability rises over time.
claims.testable: no - not testable until a crisis

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the Goldman Sachs commodity index relative to the S&P it's at the lowest level it's ever been
claims.claim: The GSCI/S&P ratio is at a record low, suggesting reversion in favour of commodities against equities.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the AI demand for energy will trig will trigger a massive inflation in certain limited assets
claims.claim: AI buildout needs real energy that cannot be printed, so energy, nuclear and uranium assets (and gold, which nearly doubled) will see price inflation.
claims.indicator: energy and uranium prices; nuclear stocks

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: If these small nuclear reactors are not what we expect, then AI has to basically collapse 70 80%.
claims.claim: AI valuations depend on new energy supply (small nuclear); if it falls short, AI stocks must fall 70-80%.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: Volatility today does not measure risk.
claims.claim: Standard deviation misses risk: a stock rising 5% a day and one rising 1% a day both have zero volatility, so vol budgets are blind to some risk.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: low low volatility and high correlation between your longs and your shorts creates an opportunity to basically leverage
claims.claim: PMs size leverage from standard deviation and long-short correlation, so low vol plus high correlation allows 30x leverage.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: If you look at the skew, the rolling skew of the S&P today, it's the most negative ever.
claims.claim: Rolling S&P option skew is most negative on record, meaning options price a faster liquidity drain and vol rise on a decline, a signal ignored by hedge funds.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: alpha and high sharp ratio are 80 90% correlated to negative skew
claims.claim: Reported alpha and high Sharpe are 80-90% correlated to negative skew, so negative skew mostly explains strong Sharpe ratios.
claims.testable: yes - correlate Sharpe with skew across managers

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: be able to be long volatility while actually generating returns
claims.claim: If everyone sells tail risk for Sharpe, one can arbitrage different volatility measures to hold long-vol exposure and still earn returns.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: when volatility is low relative to the other other measures of risk effectively trade short-term breakouts
claims.claim: When standard-deviation volatility is low relative to other risk measures (ATR, price range), trade short-term breakouts in delta-1 markets, a way to buy insurance via momentum.
claims.indicator: ATR vs standard deviation; vol behavior at highs and lows

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: trading momentum in all compressed uh regimes or in all compressed markets
claims.claim: Trading momentum in vol-compressed markets produced alpha vs the S&P and the CTA index over 25 years while keeping positive convexity.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: It's been losing money effectively since it was uh created.
claims.claim: The short-term CTA index has lost money since inception while long-term (12-month momentum) strategies made money, so CTA returns differ sharply by horizon.
claims.indicator: short-term CTA index vs long-term trend indices

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the majority of the assets in the CTA industry are allocated to very very long-term CTAs with biases that reduce their ability to make returns during equity corrections.
claims.claim: CTA assets sit in long-horizon, risk-parity-like funds with long bond/equity bias, so the industry gives less protection in equity corrections.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: supplemented their momentum strategies with long equity positions
claims.claim: CTAs that did well in the last 15 years added long equity or vol-selling to momentum, i.e. rewarded style drift, which hurts the diversifier role.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: more positively skewed the strategy is the lower the sharp ratio in the last 15 years
claims.claim: In the last 15 years a more positively skewed (long convexity) strategy had a lower Sharpe, so skew is the main differentiator of CTA Sharpe and portfolio fit.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: being long volatility has been a horrible strategy in the last 15 years
claims.claim: Long-vol and short-horizon (long-convexity) exposure has performed poorly since the GFC, which drove capital away from them.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: first commodities got pinned, second FX got pinned in the 80s, fixed income got pinned in the '9s and early 2000s
claims.claim: Governments successively suppressed volatility in commodities, then FX, then fixed income, with inflation now limiting rates and stocks the last pinned asset, which pushed CTAs to drift.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: from long the long side effectively the short the short side uh doesn't make money very often
claims.claim: 80-90% of CTA returns come from the long side; shorts rarely pay, so CTAs have become long-only-like and can be replicated.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: In the full cycle, a skew is not a predictor of returns in the full cycle. In the short-term cycle, it seems that negative skew is a predictor of returns.
claims.claim: Negative skew predicts returns only in the short recent cycle, not over the full cycle, a research trap.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if you look at the rolling skew of the CTA index, it's actually flat.
claims.claim: CTAs moved from long to short tails, so the rolling skew of the CTA index is flat and it no longer diversifies portfolios.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: We want to use the data to tell us where to select the parameters
claims.claim: Modern trend followers choose horizons by data rather than committee, so a drift to longer horizons reflects what data supports.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: had not made money since September 2003 other than the risk-free rate
claims.claim: The CTA index earned only the risk-free rate from September 2003 until 2022, so the 15-year view reflects a long weak period too.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: should you optimize based on the factors are working now or should you optimize on the 100year cycle or the 50ear cycle
claims.claim: Optimising on the last 15 years (market up 16% a year vs 7% normal) is a short-term optimisation; long-cycle factor exposure is the alternative.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: we use sharp ratio as a pred predictor of asset flows
claims.claim: Sharpe ratio predicts asset flows and regime shifts because investors chase recent Sharpe, so factors and PMs that did well get reallocated to.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we will pick up a change in market regime at some point if we are data driven
claims.claim: Pure price-based trend followers will adapt to a regime change as data shifts without needing to predict it.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if value hasn't done well and value starts to do well again we're going to buy the breakout in value
claims.claim: Buy the breakout in a factor (e.g. value) when a long-underperforming factor begins to do well, as an adaptive way to catch turns.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: markets have become more efficient back in the 80s you know people didn't respond as quickly to the news
claims.claim: CTAs argue fast breakouts worked in the 70s-80s but degraded after costs as markets became more efficient and respond faster to news.
claims.indicator: short-term breakout returns net of cost

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: we're still trading commodities, we're still trading FX, we're still trading fixed income and equities all the same way with the same risk allocation
claims.claim: The firm kept equal risk allocation across sectors (long-cycle factor exposure) rather than dropping sectors that did poorly in recent years, avoiding recency optimisation.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: daily options has created the opportunity for people who are not convexity conscious to make a lot of money
claims.claim: Selling daily options gives very high Sharpe in this regime (Jane Street India case), a short-term distortion that creates short-term volatility and mean reversion.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: if you trade the inverse of a volatility breakout, if the market is up a lot, sell it.
claims.claim: In the very short term the S&P mean reverts: fading large daily moves works, unlike in other markets.
claims.direction: sell large up days, buy large down days

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the S&P cannot go up as fast as it wants. It has like a massive price pinning mechanism
claims.claim: Heavy covered call selling for yield pins the S&P and suppresses upside volatility.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: you can go long insurance and actually get paid because the call implied volatility at this point is too
claims.claim: Because call implied vol is too low from call overwriting, buying calls is cheap insurance that mean reverts if the distortion unwinds.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: Um one very important thing to to understand the real vulnerability of long-term CTAs is to look at the returns without fixed income.
claims.claim: Fixed income gave long-term CTAs positive skew; in a large inflation regime that contribution may vanish, so CTA convexity should be tested ex fixed income.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: it can also be a nice contributor like in 2022 on the short side
claims.claim: Trend followers can profit in inflation regimes via short bond positions as in 2022.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: I think of them as the LTC LTCMs of 2025.
claims.claim: Multi-manager platforms resemble LTCM: they underwrite large tail risk with large leverage for short-term high Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: What we will do is look for high sharp ratios on a time series perspective or cross-sectionally and try to short the high sharp ratios once the turnaround happens
claims.claim: Short single-stock factors whose Sharpe is abnormally high once the turn begins, as platforms feed self-reinforcing vol compression in them.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the platforms have a very specific mandate and it's to cut off PMs that are losing money and to add to PMs that I have made money
claims.claim: Platforms cut losing PMs and add to winners, so factors that performed well get reallocated to, creating distortions in single-stock factors.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: we're relatively small at 2 billion. We can actually uh trade in a time frame which is not available to the large platforms
claims.claim: Smaller capital ($2bn) can trade short horizons unavailable to large platforms, allowing trading against them.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: Our brains are not designed to uh to have a long-term perspective.
claims.claim: Short memory and chasing recent rewarded behavior create market inefficiencies; avoiding them needs long-term data and self-awareness.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: every quant researcher has the ability to uh look at the long-term cycles and take those into account
claims.claim: Quant researchers should use long cycles in their data, not only the last 15 years that dominate the available data.

claims.speaker: Nicole Kajin
claims.quote: the crowd is a very safe place to be emotionally for humans
claims.claim: Being with the crowd feels safe but is dangerous; investors must neutralise this bias.
